title: Perform Small Stock Slaughtering Procedures in an Abattoir Taking Animal Welfare into Account

lessons.title: Handling sheep and goats from truck to restrainer
lessons.html:
Welfare comes first

In this practical module you learn to slaughter sheep and goats in a way that keeps suffering to a minimum. The Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962 makes cruelty a crime, and the meat safety rules require humane handling and slaughter.

Step 1: Off-loading

  1. Check the animals on the truck. Report any dead, down, injured or very weak animals to the supervisor and meat inspector before off-loading.
  2. Open the gate and let the animals walk down the ramp on their own. Sheep follow a leader.
  3. Never throw animals off the truck or pull them by the wool, horns, legs or tail.

Step 2: Lairage

  1. Put animals in pens by owner and group, without overcrowding.
  2. Check that each pen has clean water.
  3. Record pen number, owner and count.
  4. Let them rest and wait for the meat inspector's ante-mortem inspection.

Step 3: Moving to the restrainer

  1. Move small groups, quietly, with a flag or rattle.
  2. Use the flight zone: step towards the animals' shoulder to move them forward; step back to slow them.
  3. Remove distractions: shadows, shiny water, people in front of the race.
  4. Do not overfill the race. Animals that wait too long become stressed.

Handling a sheep by hand

Hold the sheep with one hand under the jaw and the other at the back of the body or the dock. Never lift a sheep by its wool; this bruises the meat and hurts the animal. Hold goats by the neck or a collar, not only by the horns.

lessons.title: Stunning, shackling and bleeding: practical steps
lessons.html:
Before the shift

  • Check the stunner: cables, tongs or bolt, and that it is working as your plant checks it.
  • Check that a back-up stunner is ready and close by.
  • Check shackles, hoist and the sterilizer.
  • Put on your PPE: apron, boots, cut-resistant glove.

Stunning

  1. Let one animal at a time into the restrainer.
  2. Place the electrical tongs firmly in the correct position on the head, as trained, or position the captive bolt correctly for goats and horned rams.
  3. Apply for the time set by your plant. Do not change settings.
  4. Check the signs of an effective stun: collapse, no rhythmic breathing, no blinking when the eye is touched, no attempt to lift the head.
  5. If there is any doubt, stun again at once with the back-up stunner and tell the supervisor.

Shackling and hoisting

  1. Place the shackle on one hind leg straight after the stun.
  2. Hoist the animal onto the bleeding rail.
  3. Keep the time from stun to bleed short, as your plant procedure sets.

Bleeding

  1. Use a sharp, sterilised knife.
  2. Cut the main blood vessels in the neck or chest quickly and completely, as trained.
  3. Put the knife in the sterilizer; use your second knife for the next animal.
  4. Allow the full bleeding time before work starts on the carcass.
  5. Check for signs of life before dressing. If there are any, re-stun immediately.

Safety

Stunned animals kick. Stand to the side. Cut away from your body. Keep cables dry.

lessons.title: Monitoring welfare and solving problems
lessons.html:
Watching for welfare problems

A good slaughterer keeps watching the animals, not only the knife. These are signs that something is wrong:

SignPossible causeAction
Animals refuse to enter the raceShadows, noise, people in the wayFind and remove the cause; do not use force
Animals bleating and slippingWet or slippery floor, rushingSlow down; report the floor
Animal shows breathing or blinking after stunPoor tong position or equipment faultRe-stun at once; tell the supervisor
Poor bleedingIncomplete cut or long stun-to-stick timeCheck technique; tell the supervisor
Injured animal in a penTransport or fightingReport at once for emergency action

Emergency slaughter

Animals that are badly injured and suffering must not wait. Your abattoir has an emergency procedure. Tell the supervisor and meat inspector immediately and follow their instructions.

Your responsibilities

  • Use only the equipment you are trained and authorised for.
  • Never take shortcuts that cause suffering, even when the line is busy.
  • Report any cruelty you see.
  • Keep the slaughter area clean and the knives sterile.

Key points

  • Off-load and move sheep and goats calmly; never lift them by the wool or horns.
  • Check the stunner and back-up stunner before every shift.
  • Check every animal for an effective stun and re-stun at once if in doubt.
  • Bleed quickly with a sharp, sterilised knife.
  • Find and remove the causes of balking instead of using force.
  • Report injured animals and cruelty immediately.

quiz.question: How should you hold a sheep by hand?

options.text: By the wool on its back
One hand under the jaw and one at the back of the body

quiz.question: Sheep refuse to enter the race. What should you do?

options.text: Find and remove the cause, such as shadows or people in the way
Lift them into the race by the wool

quiz.question: What should you check before the shift starts?

options.text: The stunner, the back-up stunner, shackles and sterilizer
Nothing; equipment is checked once a year

quiz.question: Which stunning method is often used for goats and horned rams?

options.text: An incomplete cut or a long time between stunning and sticking

quiz.question: A badly injured, suffering animal must be reported immediately for emergency action.
When the line is very busy, it is acceptable to skip checking for an effective stun.
Which are signs of a welfare problem? (select all that apply)

options.text: Animals walking calmly into the race
An injured animal in a pen
